implementation_notes: TypeORM maps STI declaratively: @TableInheritance({ column: { type: 'varchar', name: 'type' } }) on the parent entity plus @ChildEntity() on each subclass stores the whole hierarchy in one table named after the parent, and MikroORM expresses the same idea with discriminatorColumn/discriminatorMap on the topmost entity. The mapper is metadata-driven, so the discriminator values become part of the runtime model; TypeScript's own type system does not make the type column load-bearing, so the schema contract must be declared and migrated explicitly. The hand-written form (a discriminated union plus a kind column over pg/knex) is the fallback when no decorator-based ORM is available.
pitfalls: TypeORM needs experimentalDecorators/emitDecoratorMetadata and a metadata-capable tsconfig; without them the mapping fails at startup rather than at compile time.
The discriminator is a database string derived from the entity name: renaming a child entity changes what is written, so existing rows need a data migration or an explicit discriminator value.

TypeScript's structural typing means an object carrying all columns type-checks as any subclass, so only the runtime discriminator prevents a Photo-shaped row from being loaded as a Question - do not rely on the type system to police the hierarchy.
Mixing several ORMs or raw queries against the same table bypasses the metadata, and rows with unmapped discriminator values fail at load time.
